text:
Gap G4 has no rule in the specs yet. The code and specs say the opposite of what AC 7 and 10 need.

`gap_finding`: In `plugins/temperspec-tgraph/docs/specs/session-record-checks.spec.md`, SRC-B5 (lines 46-54) and SRC-AC7 (line 96) read only "the session record". They say nothing about a visit or its retries. The Purpose (line 5) defines the record as "the tool calls of the attempt's session that the engine gives a check (CHK-B24)". Two statements pin the check to the retry session alone:
- SRC-B1's last scenario (line 18) has a retry that opens no rule file fail naming each of them.
- SRC-AC3 (line 91) says "The check after a retry attempt reads only the retry session's calls".

The engine rule is in `plugins/tempergraph/docs/specs/check-contract-and-command-runs.spec.md`. CHK-B24's scenario (line 21) says that after a retry of the same visit, `session` lists only the retry's calls. Its scenario at line 22 says a session restarted after `broken_pipe` lists only the calls since the second start. CHK-AC15 (line 194) states the same. CHK-B25 (lines 26-33) gives `None` when there is no record.

In the code, `plugins/temperspec-tgraph/workflow/temperspec/checks.py:106-124` (`_record`) takes `ctx.session`, the attempt's calls, and returns `None` when there is none. A read, edit or write call with no target also gives `None`. `_opened_rows` (lines 203-224) builds `seen` from that one record, keeping calls with capability `read` and `ok` true. It fails each row whose existing file is not in `seen`, with one finding per row and the row's path as the location. `ctx.visit` exists (used at line 629), but nothing in `_opened_rows` uses it. The criterion text is `expand.spec.md:17`, and the test helper is `tests/test_session_record_checks.py:197`.

The per-attempt scope belongs to the engine spec, so a visit-wide count needs a rule in the package spec. A change to the engine rule would break SRC-AC3 and CHK-B24.

Nothing in `docs/specs/` states a rule of the retries of one visit for `ts-exp-opened`.

Code: plugins/temperspec-tgraph/workflow/temperspec/checks.py `_record` (106-124) returns ctx.session (the attempt's calls), or None if there is none or a read/edit/write call has no target. `_opened_rows` (203-224) builds `seen` from that one record (capability read, ok true), and gives one fail finding per row whose existing file is not in `seen`, located at the row's path. No spec states a visit-wide rule, so the visit-wide count is a new SRC-B5 rule that contradicts SRC-AC3 and the engine's per-attempt record. Visit-wide data is not in `ctx.session`, so the engine would have to supply it.
